```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("functions/load_all.R")
dir.create("outputs", showWarnings = FALSE)
refresh <- isTRUE(params$refresh)
set.seed(42)
```

Value-of-information (VoI) analysis of the school garden model (@whitney2026garden). Front end:
`decisionSupport` (inputs as 90% CIs in `inputs/school_garden_estimate.csv`, `mcSimulation()`); back end:
`voi` (`evpi()`, `evppi()`, `evsi()`, `enbs()`, `pop_voi()`). Functions are in `functions/voi_garden.R`;
heavy results are saved in `outputs/`.

# Monte Carlo simulation and decision problems

Two decision problems, private and public schools, each choosing between no garden (payoff 0 by
construction, since NPVs are relative to it), a garden, and a garden with STEM education.

```{r mc}
garden_mc <- run_garden_mc(n = 1e4, seed = 42)
x <- garden_inputs(garden_mc)
decisions <- garden_decisions(garden_mc)
knitr::kable(t(sapply(decisions, colMeans)), digits = 0, caption = "Expected NPV by option (million VND)")
```

# EVPI: the value of removing all uncertainty

```{r evpi}
evpi_tab <- evpi_table(decisions)
knitr::kable(evpi_tab, digits = 1)
```

# EVPPI: which inputs matter

Single inputs, regression-based (`voi::evppi()`, default `gam`).

```{r evppi-single}
single_evppi <- cached_csv("outputs/evppi_single.csv", evppi_single_all(decisions, x), refresh)
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(split(single_evppi, single_evppi$school), head, 8)),
             digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Eight largest single-input EVPPIs per school type (million VND)")
```

Almost all single-input EVPPIs are close to zero although the EVPI is large. Two likely reasons (not tested
separately here): the plain garden is best in most of the input space, so no single input changes the
decision often; and much of the EVPI is irreducible randomness inside each run (`chance_event()` and `vv()`
draws), which no parameter study can resolve.

## Signal or noise?

Bootstrap standard errors (`evppi(se = TRUE)`) and two other regression methods for the five largest inputs
of each school type:

```{r evppi-robust}
robust <- cached_csv("outputs/evppi_robustness.csv", evppi_robustness(decisions, x, single_evppi), refresh)
knitr::kable(robust, digits = 2)
```

Only `bureaucratic_barriers` (public schools) is more than two standard errors above zero. The regression
residuals of the largest public-school input can be checked with `voi::check_regression()`:

```{r check-regression, fig.height = 6}
top_public <- single_evppi$input[single_evppi$school == "public"][1]
fit <- voi::evppi(decisions$public, x, pars = top_public, check = TRUE)
voi::check_regression(fit)
```

## Grouped EVPPI

```{r evppi-groups}
groups <- garden_input_groups(x)
group_evppi <- cached_csv("outputs/evppi_groups.csv", evppi_groups_table(decisions, x, groups, evpi_tab), refresh)
knitr::kable(group_evppi, digits = 2)
```

# EVSI, population value and net benefit of sampling

An illustrative study surveys `n` public schools to learn how often bureaucratic barriers stop a garden
(`barrier_study()`, a binomial data generator for `voi::evsi()`). The study cost (2 + 0.5 per school surveyed,
million VND), the 5-year horizon and the 5% continuous discount rate are **assumptions for illustration**.
The number of schools that would use the result is not taken from any source: a grid is shown and the
break-even number of schools is solved for.

```{r evsi}
if (refresh || !file.exists("outputs/evsi_breakeven_schools.csv")) {
  survey <- barrier_survey_value(decisions, x)
  write.csv(survey$studies, "outputs/evsi_bureaucratic_barriers.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(survey$enbs_best, "outputs/enbs_by_population.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(survey$breakeven, "outputs/evsi_breakeven_schools.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
studies <- read.csv("outputs/evsi_bureaucratic_barriers.csv")
knitr::kable(studies, digits = 2, caption = "EVSI per school, cost and net value by survey size (million VND)")
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/enbs_by_population.csv"), digits = 1,
             caption = "Best survey size and expected net benefit of sampling, by number of schools deciding")
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/evsi_breakeven_schools.csv"), digits = 2,
             caption = "Number of schools that must use the result for each survey to break even")
```

EVSI is per school and noisy (it is not monotonic at small `n`, and should not exceed the EVPPI of
`bureaucratic_barriers`, which has a standard error of about 0.9), so the break-even numbers are an order of
magnitude only.

# Pareto-optimal draws of the Monte Carlo sample

A post hoc view of the sampled outcomes (economic return, child health, biodiversity): which draws are not
dominated on all three objectives at once (`rPref::psel()`).

```{r pareto-mc}
pf <- list(garden = mc_pareto_set(garden_mc$y$NPV_garden, garden_mc$y$health, garden_mc$y$biodiversity),
           garden_STEM = mc_pareto_set(garden_mc$y$NPV_garden_STEM, garden_mc$y$health_STEM, garden_mc$y$biodiversity))
pareto_mc_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pf), function(o) data.frame(
  option = o, n_pareto = nrow(pf[[o]]), econ_median = median(pf[[o]]$economic_return),
  health_median = median(pf[[o]]$child_health), biodiversity_median = median(pf[[o]]$biodiversity))))
write.csv(pareto_mc_summary, "outputs/pareto_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(pareto_mc_summary, digits = 1)
write.csv(evpi_tab, "outputs/evpi.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
